title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

errors: No real error. Sign and normalization conventions (∂ = Σ(-1)^i d_i; normalized versus unnormalized cochains) are left implicit.

The commutative square only gives a de Rham isomorphism once one also knows Γ(X, A^n_X) = RΓ(X, A^n_X), i.e. Γ-acyclicity or extendability of each simplicial module A^n_* in Sullivan's sense. This page assumes it tacitly; the next page invokes it.
Notation slip: C^*(X_*, M_*) is written for C^*(X_*, M), the constant coefficient.

ideas.what: Yoneda/coinduction identification: maps of simplicial modules A^n_* → C^n(Δ^•, M) correspond to linear maps A^n_n → M (evaluation on the fundamental simplex).
ideas.modern_name: Representability/coinduction of simplicial cochains; integration map determined by its value on the top simplex
ideas.usually_credited_to: Implicit in Whitney, Sullivan (1977), Bousfield–Gugenheim (1976), Dupont (1976), H. Cartan 'Théories cohomologiques' (1976)

ideas.what: 'Condition de Stokes' k_n ∂_{n+1} = k_{n+1} d characterizing chain maps from a simplicial cochain complex A^• to simplicial cochains C^•(Δ^•, M).
ideas.modern_name: Abstract Stokes/integration map; de Rham–Sullivan integration morphism

ideas.what: Extension of a Stokes system to arbitrary simplicial sets X, realizing the canonical map Γ(X, A_X) → RΓ(X, A_X) ≅ RΓ(X, M) at chain level; an isomorphism when A is a resolution of M with k_0 = id on M.
ideas.modern_name: Simplicial de Rham theorem (polynomial/PD forms) via integration
ideas.usually_credited_to: Sullivan, Bousfield–Gugenheim, Dupont, Cartan (1976); integral/PD versions: Cenkl–Porter (c. 1981)

ideas.what: Use of the divided-power de Rham complex of the algebraic simplices over an arbitrary ring as the coefficient system A^•_* (context of the cote).
ideas.modern_name: Integral de Rham theorem with divided-power polynomial forms
ideas.usually_credited_to: Cenkl–Porter (tame/PD forms over Z); related to Cartan 1976

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up an axiomatic de Rham theorem: any complex of simplicial modules with a Poincaré lemma plus a Stokes system k_n gives a chain-level realization of RΓ(X, M) for every simplicial set X. Combined with the next page's existence criterion (vanishing conditions a–c), this yields integration maps without explicit formulas, e.g. for divided-power forms over Z. It is essentially contemporaneous with Cartan's 1976 axiomatics, so it is likely not new, but it is an independent Grothendieck treatment that is not documented.
missed.quote: la condition que les u_n définissent bien un hom. de complexes est la "condition de Stokes" k_n ∂_{n+1} = k_{n+1} d
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is a clean, coefficient-free formulation relevant to integral and p-adic models of cochains (divided-power forms as models of integral homotopy types). It is also a historical witness that Grothendieck worked on integral rational-homotopy-type models in 1976.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics on the page is a neat but essentially formal Yoneda/Stokes observation, close to H. Cartan's 1976 axiomatics and Sullivan/Dupont. Its interest lies mainly in documenting Grothendieck's independent, integral (divided-power) approach to the simplicial de Rham theorem.
transcription_corrections: 'Sous ces conditions, les u_α [?] X_*' should read roughly: 'Sous ces conditions, les u_n définissent, pour tout X_* ∈ ob Δ̂, un hom. déduit de u'.
Top-right target is written C^*(X_*, M_*); the intended coefficient is the constant M.
In the commutative square the left-hand crossed-out symbol before Γ is a struck 'ℝ'; the right vertical arrow is marked ≀ (isomorphism).
'Si A^* est une résolution de M_*, et k_0 : A^0_0 → M induit l'identité sur M ⊂ A^0_0': the transcription is correct.
